Left: ann and bob form one whole side of the split, so is_bipartite_node_set returns True. Right: ann and talk are three hops apart along the accent path, so they sit on opposite sides; talk (accent) breaks the set and the call returns False." width="100%"} A bipartite graph can be 2-colored, and in each connected component the two colors are fixed up to swapping. This method checks that `nodes` takes exactly one color class in every component, so that it (and the remaining nodes) form a valid two-sided split. Use it to validate the "top" side passed to bipartite methods, especially on disconnected graphs where several splits are possible. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The candidate side, as IDs or labels. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if every component's bipartition puts `nodes` entirely on one side (isolated nodes may go either way). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `nodes` repeats a node, a node does not exist, or the graph is not bipartite. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Each component is 2-colored by breadth-first search and compared with `nodes`, in $O(V + E)$. Matches NetworkX's `bipartite.is_bipartite_node_set`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#0d7e7415 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["ann", "bob", "party", "talk"]) g.add_edges([("ann", "party"), ("bob", "party"), ("bob", "talk")]) g.is_bipartite_node_set(["ann", "bob"]), g.is_bipartite_node_set(["ann", "talk"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: :::
